oneOf.description: The newest events, newest run first.

EventsView.description:
Which of a session's events a history request returns (client protocol
1.59.0; see [`crate::display_view`]).

oneOf.description:
What a transcript shows: bookkeeping left out, a superseded ACP
command list or tool presentation dropped, tool results without
their metadata, and a tool result over
[`crate::display_view::CUT_ABOVE_BYTES`] cut to its first bytes.

cursor_timestamp.description:
Timestamp of the event at `cursor` as the caller received it. When the
session's event there differs (a revert cut the log and reused the
sequence), the result is `stale_cursor` instead of events.

from.description:
`tail` (client protocol 1.59.0): answer with the newest events within
`max_bytes`, a [`HistoryWindow`], and the live tail, instead of
paging forward from `cursor`. It takes no `cursor`,
`cursor_timestamp`, or `limit`.

limit.description:
Most events to return. The server may end a page sooner to bound its
size, but a page always holds at least one event while any remain.
When more remain after them, the result sets `has_more` and registers
no live tail; the client asks again from the last returned sequence.
Only the final page subscribes.

max_bytes.description:
The byte budget of a `tail` answer's events, measured before
compression: [`HISTORY_WINDOW_DEFAULT_BYTES`] when absent, at most
[`HISTORY_WINDOW_MAX_BYTES`].

view.description:
Which events the history holds (client protocol 1.59.0): every
stored event, or the display view, which leaves out what no client
shows and cuts long tool results. Live events are sent whole either
way.
